messages:
priya: Kicking off incremental canary for release/2026-03-20-infer-v1.2-rc3. Target flow: 5% -> 15% -> 50% with 3m and 10m bakes. Pinning config to rc3. @jamal you're infra lead for this window.

deploy-bot: [DEPLOY] release/2026-03-20-infer-v1.2-rc3 started. initial_canary=5% regions=[us-west-2,us-east-1] rollout_id=rl-20260320-01

sasha: quick smoke: read/write health checks passing on canary instances, 200/200 for last 30s.

jamal: infra telemetry — p50 latency baseline=82ms, canary p50=95ms, p95 baseline=310ms, canary=330ms. CPU/mem normal. No OOMs.

monitor-bot: anomaly-detector: error_rate increased to 0.9% on canary for window=2m (baseline 0.2%). threshold=0.5%.

priya: That's above our threshold. Holding at 5%. @infra-oncall please investigate error logs and KV cache behavior.

infra-oncall: digging into logs now. Initial suspicion: a subset of canary pods showing increased 5xx tied to cold K/V cache misses during startup. Pulling pod logs.

jamal: confirmed — new pool nodes had high cache miss ratio, causing transient retries. Applying mitigation: increase cache warmup and rollout restart of affected pool.

devopsbot: ran command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-service --namespace=prod-canary --selector=pool=canary-v2` — restart started.

sasha: post-restart: error_rate down to 0.15% for 4m, p95 latency back within +5% of baseline. All smoke tests green. Recommend proceed to 15%.

priya: Good catch. Proceeding to 15% now. Starting 3m watch. Change window locked until 21:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: [TRAFFIC] shifted canary -> 15% (rollout_id=rl-20260320-01).

monitor-bot: health-checks: all systems nominal for 6m. No regression alerts. :white_check_mark:

priya: If we stay green for the 10m bake after 15%, we plan to move to 50%. Drafting release notes and rollback playbook: https://confluence.company/release/2026-03-20-infer-v1.2-rc3 (internal).

jamal: I'll keep the pin on rc3 and watch error_rate. If we exceed 0.7% or see sustained latency delta >20% we'll revert to v1.1 (pinned).

priya: Agreed. Thanks everyone — please call this thread if you see any new anomalies. :thumbsup:
